hourly.summary: Manchester United fans are greeting the Pochettino era with a toxic cocktail of gallows humor and grim resignation. The club's worst start since 1986, a billion-pound Glazer debt millstone, and a carousel of sporting directors have left supporters historically numb — yet the Argentine's appointment brings a sliver of 'now the excuses run out' pressure. The Sporting CP ties (Ronaldo, Bruno, Amorim) only sharpen the knife of what could've been.

daily.summary: Sentiment showed a modest intraday improvement from 'Shambolic' (4/10) to 'Hopium' (6/10) as Pochettino's first day at Carrington briefly lifted spirits, though deep-seated Glazer distrust, transfer farce, academy exits, and on-pitch chaos kept the overall mood fragile. The dominant narrative remains cynical resignation punctuated by fleeting optimism.

weekly.summary: Fan sentiment began in existential crisis (2/10) with the club in the relegation zone and ownership rage dominant, briefly lifted by Pochettino rumors (4/10) before crashing again on Carrick's sacking (2/10). His appointment brought apprehensive hope (4-5/10) that quickly faded into disillusionment (3/10), finally settling into a dark, resigned acceptance of mediocrity (5/10) laced with gallows humor. The week traces an arc from acute despair through false dawns to cynical resignation, with structural anger at the Glazers/INEOS ownership remaining the constant undercurrent.
